raw_signal_observation: The current validation/repair path explicitly keeps background-sync repair non-interactive while the sp_op_log lock is held. The source comments state that blocking native dialogs inside that lock are unsafe and that repair-operation creation also defaults to non-interactive in this context.
material_claim: Silent/non-interactive repair during the held background-sync lock is an explicit technical invariant, not missing UX by itself. Reintroducing a blocking confirmation at that point would violate the lock-safety contract; any transparency intervention must be deferred until after the lock or use a non-blocking path.
neta_next_move: Preserve the non-interactive in-lock repair invariant. If product policy requires explicit user acknowledgement, design it after lock release or as non-blocking telemetry/UI; do not restore native confirm inside the critical section.
reversal_condition: If the lock is removed from this path or a new dialog mechanism is proven not to block the lock/event-loop contract, reassess whether acknowledgement can safely occur inline.
baseline_decision: DEFER/REFINE: do not place blocking confirm() inside the sync lock; if users need visibility into automatic repairs, surface a non-blocking notification after the critical section.

evidence: Post-freeze issue #9026, opened by a project collaborator, documents that blocking confirm() inside sp_op_log caused real 30-second lock-acquisition timeouts and a roughly 10-minute blocked field interval.
Issue #9026 explicitly recommends not prompting while holding sp_op_log and/or using a non-blocking dialog after release, matching the current source invariant.
adjudication.decision_delta: NO_MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: both Neta and baseline preserved the same lock-safety boundary. The case confirms the local mechanism but does not add marginal decision value over baseline.
adjudication.lesson: Anti-build is not the only valid discipline: when source carries an explicit invariant backed by a prior field failure, the correct move may simply be to preserve it. Strong source comments can encode real operational knowledge without granting claims outside that mechanism.
